page: Amazon Web Services r6a.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance powered by third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors operating at up to 3.6 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 128 dedicated virtual CPUs across 64 physical cores alongside 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware architecture yields an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is rated at a 50 Gbps baseline. There is no bundled local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU acceleration, meaning workloads rely entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core computational and memory throughput. The server scores in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests (191,194.18) and PassMark CPU evaluations (99,463.44), supported by strong cryptographic capability via AES and VAES instruction sets. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 252.99 GB/sec, while in-memory throughput is demonstrated by a top-tier Redis score of 136.38 million SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1725.0) and bzip3 decompression, perform in the middle 50% tier. Instruction extensions exclude AVX-512 and AMX flags, which limits efficiency for specific vector computation tasks.

The r6a.32xlarge delivers solid resource density for enterprise workloads requiring extensive RAM footprint and heavy parallel execution. Without local disks, disk-intensive workloads will depend on network storage latency and bandwidth configurations. This server is best suited for large in-memory databases such as Redis or Memcached, distributed enterprise caching tiers, large-scale data analytics processing engines, memory-intensive electronic design automation, and high-concurrency relational database deployments.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs from 64-core AMD EPYC 7R13 processors running at 3.6 GHz, backed by 1024 GB of DDR4 memory and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Operating on the AWS Nitro System, it provides an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio tailored for memory-bound workloads. Synthetic benchmarks show top-tier multi-core computing and memory performance, registering 136.38 million Redis SET operations per second and top-decile PassMark CPU scores. The platform omits local disk storage and GPU hardware, and its instruction set lacks AVX-512 extensions. As a result, the instance presents balanced compute-to-memory density optimal for in-memory databases, large distributed caches, enterprise relational databases, and high-throughput data processing platforms.
